nodes.name: Sort Emails Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Align Field Names

# Build a weekly summary on a schedule

**Pattern:** Scheduled Digest · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers inbox-triage work end to end across Google Sheets, Telegram and Slack.

It moves through 17 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Gather from Google Sheets
3. Gather from Google Sheets 2
4. Blend Sources
5. Roll Up KPIs
6. Compose HTML Report
7. Send Report via Telegram
8. Cap Batch Volume
9. Tag Pipeline Metadata
10. Guard Non-Empty from
11. Save Execution Metadata
12. Sort Emails Newest First
13. Align Field Names
14. Stamp Processing Time
15. Summarize Run Stats
16. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
17. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Telegram — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing inbox-triage work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Gather from Google Sheets → Gather from Google Sheets 2 → Blend Sources → Roll Up KPIs → Compose HTML Report → Send Report via Telegram → Cap Batch Volume → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Guard Non-Empty from → Save Execution Metadata → Sort Emails Newest First → Align Field Names → Stamp Processing Time → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Telegram

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Telegram aligned by hand for inbox triage
- Inbox triage work where "Gather from Google Sheets" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Inbox triage work that only reaches Google Sheets on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Telegram in step for inbox triage, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Google Sheets or Telegram call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 19 nodes in this inbox-triage build
- Branches rejoin before Google Sheets, so a inbox-triage run reports once rather than 19 times
- Every inbox-triage run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Google Sheets
- Fans the same result out to Slack in the same run, for inbox triage

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; Slack OAuth2; Telegram bot token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

KPIs are rolled up with Summarize (exact group-by + aggregate) before any AI touches the data — asking an LLM to 'figure out the numbers' from raw records is slower, costlier, and less reliable than doing exact arithmetic in n8n and only asking the model to narrate numbers that are already correct.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Add a second data source and watch it blend into the same report via Merge.
2. Toggle the AI executive-summary step on and off and compare the report's usefulness.
3. Change the KPI grouping field and see how the pivot reshapes.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Telegram bot token**
Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Get your chat ID by messaging the bot then opening api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your inbox triage process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Telegram: the bot token is a bearer credential — rotate it if it ever appears in an execution log.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

**Do not log**
inbox-triage payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
